intro: The small phrases that keep people on good terms: apologising, thanking, congratulating and sending regards.
p.perdonar.consejo: Ask forgiveness with «perdóname» (tú) or «perdone» (usted). The accent keeps the stress: per-DO-na-me.
p.disculpar.consejo: «Disculpa» (tú) and «disculpe» (usted) ask forgiveness or get someone's attention.
p.sin querer.consejo: It explains that something was an accident: «ha sido sin querer».
p.no pasa nada.consejo: It is the most common answer to an apology. Double negation is normal in Spanish.
p.gracias por.consejo: After «por» comes a noun or an infinitive: «gracias por el regalo», «gracias por venir».
p.de nada.consejo: It is the most common answer to «gracias». You also hear «no hay de qué».
p.prometer.consejo: You say «te lo prometo». After «prometer que» the future is usual: «prometo que iré».
p.felicidades.consejo: It is used at birthdays and celebrations. It is always plural: «¡felicidades!».
p.enhorabuena.consejo: It is written as one word and the h is silent: en-o-ra-BWE-na.
p.igualmente.consejo: It answers a wish or a greeting: «¡Que descanses!» – «Igualmente».
p.recuerdos.consejo: You say «dale recuerdos a…» or «te manda recuerdos». It is almost always plural.
p.de mi parte.consejo: It sends a greeting or thanks: «dale las gracias de mi parte».
p.estás en tu casa.consejo: You say it when welcoming someone. With «usted»: «está en su casa».
p.encantado de conocerte.consejo: A woman says «encantada». More formal: «mucho gusto» or «encantado de conocerle».
b1.texto:
These small phrases keep people on good terms:

- **Apologising**: **perdona** / **perdóname** (tú), **perdone** (usted), **lo siento**, **ha sido sin querer**. Replies: **no pasa nada**, **no importa**, **no te preocupes**.
- **Thanking**: **gracias por** + noun or infinitive (*gracias por venir*). Replies: **de nada**, **no hay de qué**, **a ti**.
- **Congratulating**: **¡enhorabuena!** (a success), **¡felicidades!** (a birthday), **¡que cumplas muchos más!**
- **Wishing**: **que** + subjunctive: **que descanses**, **que tengas suerte**. Reply: **igualmente**.
- **Sending regards**: **recuerdos a** your family. Reply: **de tu parte**.
- **Welcoming**: **pasa, estás en tu casa**.
- **Introducing**: **este es Luis**. **Encantado de conocerte** (encantada, if you are a woman) or, more formal, **mucho gusto**.
b2.f0.texto: Oh, sorry, it was an accident.
b2.f2.texto: Come in, make yourself at home.
b2.f5.texto: Hello, I am Andrés, Berta's cousin.
b2.f8.texto: My mother sends you her regards.
b4.texto:
Good wishes begin with **que** and take the verb in the **subjunctive**:

- **Que descanses.**
- **Que tengas suerte.**
- **Que cumplas muchos más.**
- **Que te mejores.**

After **gracias por** comes a noun or an infinitive: *gracias por el regalo*, *gracias por venir*. After **perdóname por** comes an infinitive: *perdóname por llegar tarde*.

To promise, use **te prometo que** + future: *te prometo que no volverá a pasar*.
b4.e0.texto: I hope you have lots of luck.
b4.e2.texto: I promise it will not happen again.
b5.f0.texto: The dining table gleams under the warm lights of the lamp.
b5.f1.texto: The white plates form a perfect circle around the cake.
b5.f2.texto: Thirty small candles tremble above the chocolate cream.
b5.f3.texto: The smell of chocolate mixes with the perfume of the flowers.
b5.f4.texto: In the hallway you can hear the laughter of the first guests.
b5.f5.texto: Jaime comes through the door with a parcel wrapped in golden paper.
b5.f6.texto: His wet coat smells of rain and cold streets.
b5.f7.texto: Berta hugs him tightly and takes the coat off his shoulders.
b5.f8.texto: An old song fills the room with voices and clapping.
b5.f9.texto: Everyone blows out the candles at once amid laughter and applause.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! It plays down the mistake.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Igualmente» answers a wish or greeting, not an apology.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is said by someone who commits to something. It does not fit.
b6.pregunta: Someone steps on you and says «¡Perdón!». What do you answer?
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is a command. The imperative does not follow «por».
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is a conjugated verb. After «por» you need the infinitive.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Well done! You promise to pass on the message from them.
b8.o2.refuerzo: «No importa» answers an apology. It does not fit here.
b8.pregunta: You are told «Dale recuerdos a tu padre». What do you answer?
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Wishes with «que» take the subjunctive.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is the ordinary present. A wish needs the subjunctive.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work here: a conjugated verb is missing.
b9.pregunta: Which form goes in a wish with «que»?
b10.frase: Te prometo que no volverá a pasar
b10.traduccion: I promise it will not happen again
b12.o0.refuerzo: «De tu parte» answers regards, not a wish.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Bien hecho» congratulates you for something you did. It does not fit.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Exactly! You return the same wish to the other person.
b12.pregunta: You are told «¡Que tengas un buen fin de semana!». What do you answer?
p.ay.consejo: A short exclamation of surprise or pain. Do not confuse «ay» with «hay» (there is) or «ahí» (there).
p.sido.consejo: Participle of «ser», used in «ha sido». It is the same for masculine and feminine.
p.manda.consejo: Present of «mandar». “Mandar recuerdos” is to send regards, and “mandar” also means to order.
p.dale.consejo: Command «da» + «le». It has no accent because the stress is already on the second-to-last syllable.
p.tengas.consejo: Subjunctive of «tener»: «tengo» → «tengas». It is used in wishes: «que tengas suerte».
p.suerte.consejo: It is feminine: «la suerte». “Ue” is one syllable: SWER-te. «Buena suerte» is the usual good wish.
p.perdóname.consejo: Command «perdona» + «me». The accent keeps the stress on «DO», three syllables from the end.
p.prometo.consejo: Present of «prometer» for «yo». “Te prometo que…” is followed by a verb in the future.
p.volverá.consejo: Future of «volver»: infinitive + «á». “No volverá a pasar” means “it will not happen again”.
p.pasar.consejo: Regular «-ar» verb with several meanings. In «no volverá a pasar» it means “to happen”.
p.cálidas.consejo: Feminine plural of «cálido». All words stressed on the third-to-last syllable carry an accent.
p.blancos.consejo: Masculine plural of «blanco», agreeing with «los platos». The «c» before o sounds k.
p.perfecto.consejo: The «ct» is pronounced as «k» + «t»: per-FEK-to. “Un círculo perfecto” is a flawless circle.
p.crema.consejo: It is feminine: «la crema». “Crema de chocolate” is a soft sweet spread or filling.
p.chocolate.consejo: It is masculine: «el chocolate». The «ch» is like in “cheese”, and the «c» before o sounds k.
p.mezcla.consejo: Present of «mezclar». The «z» sounds “th” in Spain: METH-kla. «Se mezcla» means it blends with something.
p.risa.consejo: It is feminine: «la risa». The initial «r» is strong: RRI-sa. The plural «risas» is common.
p.invitados.consejo: From «invitar». The «v» sounds like a b: in-bi-TA-dos. For women you say «invitadas».
p.cruza.consejo: Present of «cruzar». The «z» sounds “th” in Spain: KRU-tha. Before e it becomes «c»: «crucé».
p.envuelto.consejo: Participle of «envolver», which has an irregular form: «envuelto», not «envolvido». It agrees: «envuelta».
p.mojado.consejo: The «j» sounds like a strong h: mo-HA-do. The opposite is «seco». It agrees: «abrigo mojado», «calle mojada».
p.quita.consejo: Present of «quitar». The «qu» sounds k and the u is silent: KI-ta. “Quitar el abrigo” is to take someone's coat.
p.hombros.consejo: Plural of «el hombro». The «h» is silent: OM-bros. “Encogerse de hombros” is to shrug.
p.voces.consejo: Plural of «la voz»: the «z» changes to «c» before e. The «c» sounds “th” in Spain; the «v» sounds b.
p.palmas.consejo: Plural of «la palma». “Dar palmas” is to clap. In Spain it is also a rhythm in flamenco.
p.soplan.consejo: Third person plural of «soplar». “Soplar las velas” is the birthday custom of blowing out candles.
p.aplausos.consejo: Plural of «el aplauso». “Au” is one syllable: a-PLAU-sos. The verb is «aplaudir».
p.ayudarme.consejo: After «gracias por» you need an infinitive. The pronoun «me» joins it: «gracias por ayudarme».
p.parte.consejo: It is feminine: «la parte». In «de tu parte» it means “on your behalf”, used to pass on a message.
